office_does: A Pierce County District Court judge hears misdemeanor and gross misdemeanor cases, traffic infractions, protection orders and civil claims up to $100,000 for a four-year term; the discretion is mostly in pretrial release, sentencing and therapeutic-court supervision.
race_blurb: An open seat. Former Olympia Municipal Court judge Pam Nogueira led the August primary by 738 votes over 31-year Pierce County deputy prosecutor Mike Sommerfeld, who holds the Tacoma-Pierce County Bar's Exceptionally Well Qualified rating and has raised far more money.

candidates.summary: Attorney and judge pro tem who served as an Olympia Municipal Court judge (2023 to February 2026) and a Thurston County Superior Court commissioner (2021 to 2023). Her earlier practice included public defense and drug court defense in Grays Harbor County.
highlights: Olympia Municipal Court judge 2023 to February 2026, re-elected unopposed in November 2025; Thurston County Superior Court commissioner 2021 to 2023 [S2][S12]
Contracted public defense and drug court defense attorney in Grays Harbor County [S2]
Supports diversion, treatment courts and community-based alternatives where legally authorized, weighing victim and community safety [S5]
DMCJA Diversity co-chair, FAIR Court Project advisory board and Therapeutic Courts committee member [S2][S5]
Placed first in the primary with 36.4%; not on TPCBA's 2026 ratings list [S11][S7]

experience.basis: About five years as a full-time judicial officer (municipal judge, superior court commissioner) plus pro tem service, confirmed in part by her 2025 election; runs on a bench record, though not as an incumbent of this court.

safety.basis: Formation in public defense and drug court defense; states support for diversion, treatment courts and community-based alternatives, while saying restorative approaches are not right for every case.

judicial.basis: Says the judiciary 'must reflect the values of the community it serves'; judicial-association record on the FAIR Court Project and diversity work; supports data-driven review of outcome disparities.

candidates.summary: Pierce County deputy prosecuting attorney since 1995, about 15 years in criminal prosecution and since 2010 legal advisor to Pierce County District Court and Juvenile Court. He has served as a Thurston County District Court judge pro tem.
highlights: Pierce County deputy prosecutor since 1995; prosecuted DUI and domestic violence through murder and child sexual abuse cases [S3][S4]
Legal advisor to Pierce County District Court judges and staff since 2010; Thurston County District Court pro tem judge [S2][S3]
Says he will 'hold violent offenders accountable while expanding therapeutic and alternative programs' [S4]
Rated Exceptionally Well Qualified by the Tacoma-Pierce County Bar Association [S5]
Endorsements listed include the District Court presiding judge, the county prosecutor and executive, police and prosecutor groups, and party organizations on both sides [S2]

experience.basis: Runs on 31 years of institutional service in the county prosecutor's office, including advising this court, with pro tem bench experience; an insider record rather than an outsider case.

safety.basis: Formation is criminal prosecution; pairs 'hold violent offenders accountable' with support for therapeutic and alternative programs, a mixed stance anchored in a prosecutorial career.

judicial.basis: Questionnaire supports language access, representative juries and fee relief and says judges should be aware of historical inequities; a single questionnaire to an endorsing club, so low confidence.
